archetype: WU forced-draw punisher control with a hug-fort shell and a VERIFIED storm-kill finisher: symmetric table-draw engines feeding asymmetric hand-size punishers, Heliod, the Warped Eclipse converting opponents' draws into cost reduction and flash, and — new in v3 — the checker-passed Hullbreaker Horror + Sol Ring + Arcane Signet + Aetherflux Reservoir table-kill as the primary win line, with Grand Abolisher as its purpose-built protection and a planeswalker suite as the sweep-surviving second layer

role_assignment.default_role: control with inevitability: the punisher upkeep damage (verified stack 003: Iron Maiden + Ebony Owl Netsuke deal 7 on the punished upkeep once Forced Fruition fills the hand; cleanup trims to exactly 7) is a clock that runs without tapping out, and the counterspell suite (free/cheap interaction held by t6 in 62% of goldfish games, 73.3% ever) defends the long game. Whoever loses the long game must be the beatdown, and that is usually not you (strategy:whos-the-beatdown, strategy:whos-the-beatdown.metagame-clock). The hug-fort layer (Kwain, The Second Doctor) buys the waiting turns politically (strategy:multiplayer.politics)
role_assignment.pivot_trigger: the go decision is now concrete storm arithmetic (strategy:critical-mass.storm-math): commit the turn you can deploy Hullbreaker Horror plus both rocks and Aetherflux Reservoir in one main phase — ideally the turn after Grand Abolisher, whose static closes every priority window the verified kill (stack 006) honestly opens — or the turn Approach of the Second Sun's second cast is set up behind held countermagic (verified stack 002). Hold protection FOR the commit turn, not after (strategy:pivot-point); going early into three players' open mana is how the 15-cast line dies (strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window). Wincon access reaches 50.1% of goldfish games by t6 (61.2% ever, mean turn 3.144) now that Jace, Wielder of Mysteries counts

engines.piece: Hullbreaker Horror + Sol Ring + Arcane Signet + Aetherflux Reservoir
engines.engine: THE VERIFIED PRIMARY WIN LINE (promoted from candidate this pass). Stack 006 (checker: pass, 2 iterations) walks the complete table-kill with an exact ledger: the 004-verified mana-neutral alternating-bounce loop makes each cast n net +n life off the Reservoir's 'gain 1 life for each spell you've cast this turn' (triangular growth, the trigger-sees-n count forced by 301.1 since the sorcery-speed artifacts are only castable stack-empty); from 32 life, 15 casts is the proven minimum — casts 1-6 (+21, life 53) fund activation one, casts 7-12 (+57, life 60) fund two, casts 13-15 (+42, life 52) fund three; three 'Pay 50 life: deal 50 damage' activations kill all three opponents in one main phase via SBAs (104.5/104.2a), ending at 2 life with the loop still available. The verified weakness in the same artifact: every activation AND every loop cast opens a fully open priority window — activating is not casting, so Hullbreaker never triggers on it, and the loop pieces cannot be cast in response to anything, so the engine gives itself zero protection. Requires nothing beyond the four pieces and {2} to start
engines.evidence: verified stack 006 (full ledger, 15-cast minimum, all three deaths, open-window caveat); verified stack 004 (loop mana-neutral, unbounded); verified stack 001 (two-card form refuted); verified stack 005 (Kitten mana-positive extension refuted)

engines.engine: the protection layer the verified kill was missing — and the reason the swap matters strategically. Stack 006's honest caveat is that the kill's windows are rules-open on an unprotected board; Grand Abolisher's oracle text ('During your turn, your opponents can't cast spells or activate abilities of artifacts, creatures, or enchantments') closes exactly those windows on exactly the turn the loop runs. Sequencing rule: Abolisher the turn before, or lead the combo turn with it; failing that, the free suite (Fierce Guardianship, Force of Negation, Swan Song, An Offer You Can't Refuse, Dovin's Veto) guards the windows the hard way. This is the held-protection-on-the-commit-turn discipline made literal (strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window)
engines.evidence: oracle text (Grand Abolisher); verified stack 006 names Abolisher as the in-99 window-closer in its steps and final summary; goldfish 'Free or cheap interaction held' 62% by t6

engines.piece: Forced Fruition + Iron Maiden + Ebony Owl Netsuke
engines.engine: the punisher core: force draws (Forced Fruition, Howling Mine, Font of Mythos, Temple Bell, Dictate of Kruphix, Kami of the Crescent Moon, Folio of Fancies) into hand-size upkeep damage (Iron Maiden, Ebony Owl Netsuke, Viseling) — a two-piece critical-mass engine that is inert below threshold and a table-wide clock past it; opponents trim to seven at cleanup, so the punishers hit on upkeep before the drawn cards are spent (verified sequencing, stack 003). Deck-facts still flags most of this core as role-untagged — the histogram undercounts the real plan
engines.evidence: verified stack 003; oracle text; goldfish 'Engine + punisher assembled' 41.3% by t6 (56.5% ever, mean turn 4.154)

engines.piece: Jace Beleren + Jace, Wielder of Mysteries + Teferi, Temporal Pilgrim
engines.engine: the sweep-surviving threat layer, new in v3: planeswalkers dodge Supreme Verdict — including YOUR OWN, so you can wrath a hostile board while your walkers keep drawing. This is Duke's 'buy resilience instead of restraint' answer to sweeper exposure (strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math). Beleren's +2 feeds the punisher math and Heliod's discount from three opponents' draws; Temporal Pilgrim self-charges off every draw in a deck built on drawing (and its Spirit token grows the same way); Wielder of Mysteries is a standing wincon whose +1 draws while threatening the empty-library win, which is why goldfish wincon access rose to 50.1% by t6
engines.evidence: oracle text (all three walkers, Supreme Verdict); goldfish 'Win condition access' 50.1% by t6, 61.2% ever

engines.engine: the blink engine: every noncreature cast blinks a permanent — Sol Ring returns untapped, Mystic Remora returns with zero age counters, Loran re-triggers its ETB removal. Its tempting degenerate extension stays REFUTED: stack 005 shows the Kitten does NOT make the Hullbreaker loop mana-positive (both triggers lock targets at announcement; the blinked permanent is a new object), leaving only a one-time loop-terminating exit worth +1 float (terminal float 3). With the kill now verified through the Reservoir, the Kitten's job is value, not combo
engines.evidence: oracle text; verified stack 005 (mana-positive claim refuted; +1-float exit verified)

engines.piece: Kwain, Itinerant Meddler + The Second Doctor + Alhammarret's Archive
engines.engine: the hug-fort layer: Kwain taps for table draws (+life), The Second Doctor's end-step draw carries a rider that blanks the acceptor's next attack step against you (alongside Propaganda and Ghostly Prison), and every accepted card pushes hands toward the Iron Maiden/Netsuke thresholds. Alhammarret's Archive is the asymmetry hinge: your draws and life gain double while opponents' don't; Reliquary Tower/Thought Vessel/Second Doctor let you hoard the surplus
engines.evidence: oracle text; goldfish 'Table draw engine drawn' 75.7% by t6, mean turn 2.469

engines.engine: the hinge that makes the symmetric draw asymmetric: spells cost {1} less per card opponents drew this turn and everything gains flash, so the table-draw engines pay your mana bill and let you deploy at instant speed while holding counters — the opponents' cards working for you (strategy:card-advantage.virtual). The hug pieces directly grow the discount on the turns you want to act

matchup_frames.vs_sweeper_control: In the control mirror someone must be the beatdown (strategy:whos-the-beatdown) — and your punishers advance during draw-go, so you own inevitability (strategy:whos-the-beatdown.metagame-clock). New in v3, your board is sweep-layered on purpose: the walker suite lives through every Supreme Verdict, including yours, so the resilience Duke prescribes over restraint is built in (strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math) — the real exposure is artifact/enchantment mass removal taking engine and punisher layers together, plus Hullbreaker Horror itself dying to creature wraths; keep the kill pieces in hand until the commit turn (strategy:pivot-point). Supreme Verdict remains YOUR uncounterable reset through their permission.
matchup_frames.vs_stax: Taxes attack this deck's velocity math — many cheap spells per turn — so recount the hand under the tax (strategy:threat-assessment.resource-denial); under an assembling lock your role flips to beatdown, racing completion. Heliod's per-opponent-draw discount is a partial tax rebate the forced-draw engines keep feeding, and Kitten re-triggering Loran gives repeatable answers to lock pieces. New in v3 you are partly the denial player yourself: Drannith Magistrate shuts off opponents' commanders and every non-hand cast — a ninth Game Changer that makes YOU the lock in commander-dependent pods. Note the 15-cast kill needs only {2} and the pieces: it races most soft locks that don't stop artifact casts.
matchup_frames.vs_aggro: Propaganda, Ghostly Prison, and The Second Doctor's attack-deterrent rider are virtual card advantage tripled in multiplayer — one pillow effect blanks attack plans from three players (strategy:card-advantage.virtual) — and the punishers convert defense into a clock that pushes the aggressor's damage-per-card below lethal (strategy:life-as-resource.philosophy-of-fire). Commit little board and let them overextend into Supreme Verdict (strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math). The trap remains: Forced Fruition refuels their hand — sequence punishers before or with the big draw engines (strategy:critical-mass). One life-total caveat new to v3: the Reservoir kill pays 50 life three times, so an aggro pod that has chipped you complicates the ledger — stack 006 proves any positive total works because per-cast gain grows without bound, but lower totals need more casts and therefore more open windows.
matchup_frames.vs_combo: Hold the free suite (Fierce Guardianship, Force of Negation, Swan Song, An Offer You Can't Refuse, Dovin's Veto — held by t6 in 62% of goldfish games) for the card that ends the game, per the answer-economy bar (strategy:threat-assessment.answer-economy). V3 sharpened both directions of this matchup: Drannith Magistrate blanks their commander- and non-hand-zone lines before they start, and Grand Abolisher makes YOUR combo turn uninterruptable — you are now the faster, better-protected combo deck in many pods, which flips your role to beatdown (strategy:whos-the-beatdown). The standing warning: Forced Fruition hands a storm pilot seven cards per spell and the hug layer is a liability against spellslinger pods; and expect tables to discount your quiet artifacts and hit you anyway (strategy:multiplayer.threat-deflection).

distribution_notes: 85 entries / 100 copies, 18 land entries; curve 9/22/15/11 at MV 1-4 with ten cards at MV 5+, leaning on Heliod's discount for the top end. Pips skew hard blue: 57 U pips across 38 cards (source target 36 vs 6 U-producing lands — rocks and duals carry it) against 16 W pips across 14 (target 22); Heliod's front face is W but the operating colour is U. Goldfish v3 (seed 42, 10k iters, sha fbbb52c8): commander mean cast 4.144 (median 4, 89.8% by t6), keep-first-seven 73.6%; table draw engine by t6 75.7%, core two-piece 41.3% by t6 (56.5% ever), wincon access 50.1% by t6 — UP from 42.6% because Jace, Wielder of Mysteries now counts — and interaction held 62% by t6. Mulligan rule: engine-half hands dig toward punishers; punisher-only hands are blanks until the engine exists (strategy:mulligans.engine-hands). 23 cards including most of the punisher core carry no role tag — the histogram undercounts the plan. Bracket floor 4 (Optimized), now pinned twice over: NINE Game Changers (Drannith Magistrate joined), and the kill content is no longer just a DB claim — stack 001 refuted the listed two-card infinite, but stack 006 verifies the four-card table-kill, so the floor-4 conversation is honest either way.
overall_assessment: V3 completes this deck's identity: it is no longer a control deck with a suspected combo — it is a control deck with a VERIFIED kill. The world-view is still Duke's inevitability (strategy:whos-the-beatdown.metagame-clock): every symmetric draw is asymmetric three ways — Heliod's discount, the hand-size punishers, the Tithe/Sphinx value layer — and the hug-fort keeps the waiting game political (strategy:multiplayer.politics). But the endgame is now concrete storm arithmetic rather than attrition hope: Hullbreaker + both rocks + Aetherflux Reservoir kills all three opponents in one main phase, 15 casts minimum from 32 life, checker-passed with an exact ledger (stack 006) — and the same artifact names the line's one weakness, fully open priority windows on every cast and activation, which is precisely what Grand Abolisher, added in the same swap, exists to close (strategy:critical-mass.storm-math, strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window). The other swaps serve the same two masters: the walkers make the long game sweep-proof on both sides of your own Supreme Verdict (strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math), and Drannith adds a denial axis that doubles as a candidate stranding lock. Play it as the control deck that never has to win the long game it owns — and the moment the four pieces line up behind an Abolisher, stop playing fair (strategy:pivot-point).
